question: Can an authored local food substrate and mouth-contact uptake give the existing neural organisms enough energy and time for reproduction to occur?

scientific_search.reason: The nursery protocol registered this as an authored habitat slice. No publications were consulted, and none should be cited as support for the feeding rule or the probe.

authored_assumptions: Food sits on a fixed lattice of sites.
A mouth can take stock only from sites at distance-squared <= 2, preferring the head site and then nearer sites.
Uptake is automatic on contact. It is not a learned action.
The basic bite is 1 nutrient credited as 4 energy. Maintenance is 1. A clot starts at 512. Founders start at 128 energy. Birth still requires 256.
Smell is an 8-step weighted ray in the body facing. It is not a map.
Muscle rate, ligament stiffness, and ligament rest are germline genes on every neural organism. The muscle smooths the nerve command. The ligament springs toward the heritable curl.
With drag, a bending spine can exchange momentum with the medium. Vacuum still has no center-of-mass thrust from internal motion.
Crossing a site condenses 1 reservoir unit into permanent flesh on the vacated site. It does not fade.
No new publications were consulted for the tissue, the scent, the trail, or the bite.

evidence.deviation: Fixture birth cooldown is 32 ticks. The 256³ nursery cooldown remains 128.
